analysis: The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md. The sole change is head lines 595-611, which document a Gated DeltaNet four-row prefill recurrence kernel for qwen3_5, qwen3_5_moe and prism_hadamard_qwen35. The first prompt window of each kernel instantiation per process probes the `packed` and then the `rows` kernel against `gated_delta_step` and keeps the first that is bit-exact on the GPU, else the stock kernel. Decode, MTP verification, masked updates and windows shorter than 16 positions use the stock kernel. The `DARKBLOOM_TTFT_GDN_BLOCKED` env var overrides the choice for A/B measurement. This is documentation only, so no code, control, endpoint or deployment behavior is changed by this PR. I checked it against the threat model. T-041 (prefix cache, TTFT oracle, checkpoint capture) is relevant only through the claim that kernel mixing leaves recurrent state bit-identical for checkpoint capture. That claim concerns correctness, not a new disclosure path, and it does not alter cache scoping, HMAC naming, TTL or crypto. The env override is an operator-local tuning knob, consistent with the existing operator-controlled configuration model (TB-003). The kernel selection happens in-process, so it does not expand the coordinator trust boundary. The rest of the file is unchanged context. I saw no new attack surface or invalidated assumption. The bit-exactness and prefix-checkpoint equivalence claims rest on SDK sources not supplied (GatedDelta.swift), so I could not verify them. The next pass can confirm them against code if it matters.
